notes: Off-plan development shot flat on one overcast day, to be graded to a dusk 'blue hour' look. Two interior frames were made in a 40-minute cloud break so they carry a different illuminant and sit a stop higher in key than the four exteriors. Only ONE frame holds the complete elevation, framed tight with the parapet near the top edge at 3:2, so the wide hoarding band cannot be cropped from it (must be widened). The roof-terrace glazed pavilion sits at the value of the flat sky (fringing selection). Plus the sign-painted KV monogram on the hoarding board, the lender's landscape payment card, a 5-row units export (one withdrawn null-price type, mixed deposit units, mismatched photo filenames) and the developer notes.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the lender's flat press PDF (payment card) to be authored/rendered downstream.

Document: single page, 148 x 105 mm LANDSCAPE, 3 mm safety, fonts embedded, produced by a full layout engine (a real press PDF, not a thin hand-authored one). Shows a 2025 apartment type and 2025 figures (all now changed) so every field must be re-mapped.

GEOMETRY:
- GRAPHIC FRAME 1 (placed apartment plate/photograph): left ~48% of the card, full height inside margins, one linked image with an integer page-item id.
- GRAPHIC FRAME 2 (small placed lender wordmark): bottom-right corner, small, one linked image.
- TEXT FRAME A (right column, upper), one continuous story, runs:
    Run 1 (APARTMENT TYPE): text serif, ~16 pt. Value: "The Spindle - 2 bed"
    Run 2 (PRICE): serif, ~13 pt. Value: "From 895,000"
    Run 3 (DEPOSIT): sans, ~10 pt. Value: "Deposit 10%"
- TEXT FRAME B (right column, lower) - the regulated block, ONE continuous story with TABBED runs in this order:
    Run 4 (MONTHLY PAYMENT / SCENARIO): sans, ~10 pt, tabbed columns. Value: "Est. monthly  $3,780  over 30 yrs"
    Run 5 (RATE AND TERM - regulated disclosure): sans, ~8.5 pt, one line. Value: "Representative: 5.85% fixed 5 yrs, then 7.99% SVR. Overall cost for comparison 6.4% APRC."
    Run 6 (SMALL PRINT / CONTACT): sans, ~7.5 pt. Value: "Kestrel Home Lending. Your home may be repossessed if you do not keep up repayments. NMLS #000000."

Field labels the downstream mapping must resolve (as content, not visible tokens): APT_TYPE, PRICE, DEPOSIT, MONTHLY_PAYMENT, RATE_AND_TERM, SMALL_PRINT, PLATE, WORDMARK.

Colours: Bone Paper #EDE7DB ground, Blue Hour #22304A type, Brass #A67C3D hairline rule.

The card looks like eight stacked labelled fields; it is in fact two text frames, and the scenario/rate-and-term/small-print block is a single tabbed story. Run 5 (RATE AND TERM) is the run whose text content a lossy readout drops while keeping its trailing line break, so every offset after it runs short and the two regulated fields silently fail to become placeholders unless the story is reconstructed from the exported content runs.

assets.content:
KESTREL AND VANE - HALCYON QUARTER, NOTES FOR THE DESIGNER

What we sell is the evening. Blue hour. The water should look cold and the rooms should look warm. Brass, not gold. Nothing shiny.

Quiet and expensive. Our buyers are leaving houses they have owned for thirty years, they are not impressed by a starburst or a sunset, and they will count the windows when they visit the site. If a picture shows something the building will not have, that is the one thing we cannot survive.

Phase one is four apartment types: the Loom, the Spindle, the Ropewalk and the Warehouse. That is the set. (The Reel was pulled from phase one; if it is still in the sales export, it is not for sale yet and should not get a card.)

Kestrel Home Lending's wording on the payment cards is theirs. Every line of it, including the rate and the term and the small print, is regulated. Do not edit it, shorten it, re-space it or abbreviate it, and do not let any of it get clipped. If you cannot fit a line, tell us, do not trim it.

Type: a proper text serif with real hierarchy, prices set plainly inside the copy, generous margins, one photograph per canvas. No hex from us, no measurements, that is your craft. Just: quiet and expensive.
